item.title: Visa gets approval to prepare for domestic payments business in China
item.description: The approval marks an 'important milestone' toward the company serving China's domestic payments market, Visa said in a statement ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Paige Smith Visa Inc. received approval to begin preparations to establish a domestic bank card clearing business in China, teeing up the firm to potentially follow rivals Mastercard Inc. and American Express Co. in serving the nation’s massive payments market. The approval marks an “important milestone” toward the company serving China’s domestic payments market, Visa said in a statement. “We greatly appreciate the important role of the leaders of the United States and China in pursuing a constructive and strategically stable relationship between the world’s largest economies,” Visa Chief Executive Officer Ryan McInerney said in the statement. “For more than 40 years, Visa has been an active contributor to China’s dynamic payments landscape. We look forward to taking the necessary steps in the process, pursuant to the PBOC’s regulations, to begin operating domestically in China.”  Competitor Mastercard received approval to establish its bank card clearing business in 2020, and Amex’s joint venture in the country was approved to start bank card clearing services several months after that.  Earlier this year, US President Donald Trump said he brought up Visa’s request for access to mainland China’s market during a meeting with Xi Jinping in Beijing. Visa’s CEO McInerney accompanied Trump on that May trip to China.

item.title: Chandrasekaran defends Tata's long-term bets despite near-term uncertainty
item.description: At Bloomberg's New Economy Forum, Chandrasekaran defended chip investments and long-term capital allocation, even as differences with Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata deepen over leadership and listing ...
item.content:encoded:

Chandrasekaran defends Tata's long-term bets despite near-term uncertainty At Bloomberg's New Economy Forum, Chandrasekaran defended chip investments and long-term capital allocation, even as differences with Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata deepen over leadership and listing

Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran (Photo:PTI)

Barkha Mathur New Delhi 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 13 2026 | 12:58 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran on Tuesday defended the conglomerate's long-term investment strategy, saying the group will keep building what India and the world needs even when the benefits were not immediately visible.   Speaking at Bloomberg' s New Economy Forum in New Delhi, Chandrasekaran said semiconductor manufacturing and advanced manufacturing were critical to India's future and should not be judged solely by whether they meet targets over the next two to three years.   "There are many decisions that have been taken by various chairmen in the group which have all proved to be right in the long term," he said.   His comments come amid a growing rift between Tata Sons and its controlling shareholder, Tata Trusts , over the group's investment strategy, Chandrasekaran's own reappointment and whether the holding company should go public.

In September, the Tata Sons board reappointed Chandrasekaran for another five-year term, despite opposition from Noel Tata, chairman of Tata Trusts. The Trusts, which own about 66 per cent of Tata Sons, later termed the decision illegal, arguing that it violated the company's Articles of Association. Tata Sons has disputed this claim.   ALSO READ: Tata Trusts seeks more time to reply; Charity Commissioner grants a week   Also Read

Delhi SIR: 2 million cases resolved after EC eases voter verification rules

US visa, green card applicants face new filing deadline rules from Oct 23

NHAI mandates independent design checks for bridges, tunnels from December

From Sudha Yadav to Dushyant Gautam, meet the six newly appointed governors

Why 7-Eleven's India ambitions faltered despite Reliance Retail partnership

“Direction is certain, need is certain, ability to execute is certain,” Chandrasekaran said, referring to the group's semiconductor ambitions. “The only thing is how much you ramp up, how fast you ramp up, which technology you go to. All this is uncertain.”

“Sometimes things go wrong. Then you course-correct,” he said, adding that investments should be directed towards what India, enterprises and society need over the long term.   Chandrasekaran acknowledged that the group would need technology partners. He also cautioned against investing recklessly in advanced chip technologies without considering demand and the balance sheet.   “You can't be reckless and say that I am going to be putting a two-nanometre chip. It's just not going to work,” he said.   According to Tata Sons’ disclosures, Tata Electronics’ revenue nearly doubled to ₹1.31 trillion in FY26, but its net loss widened to ₹1,611 crore from ₹70 crore a year earlier. Its two major semiconductor projects are yet to begin production. The chip fabrication plant in Dholera, Gujarat, being built with Taiwan’s Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation, is expected to begin commercial operations in mid-2028, while the assembly and testing facility in Assam is slated to start production in December.

Resilience as a business priority Chandrasekaran said businesses should build resilience into their operations instead of focusing solely on efficiency in an unpredictable environment. He argued that the two were not mutually exclusive.   “In a highly unpredictable, volatile environment, optimising for efficiency is definitely not the right thing,” he said. “I believe that if you design for resilience in an unpredictable environment, actually you are optimising for efficiency.”   He cited shortages of magnets that can disrupt vehicle production and the cyberattack that affected Jaguar Land Rover (JLR), saying the company had almost lost six weeks of production because of the incident.   The group had also faced an air crash and supply-chain disruptions, he said, but still expected to deliver double-digit growth, with margins holding up. He did not specify the period or provide financial projections to quantify the outlook.

Chandrasekaran said he had asked companies across the group to define resilience for their own businesses rather than adopt a single framework. Geopolitical risks and technology Chandrasekaran said technology posed near-term risks, including misuse by bad actors and job restructuring, but expected it to have a far-reaching impact over the medium to long term.   He also expressed concern over the growing number of conflicts around the world, warning that wars were opening on multiple fronts without any being resolved.   "If you look at a group like ours, which is about 160 years old, we have seen two world wars, pandemics, high borrowing levels and many other things, and we have survived. So it's not the first time that something as hard as this is happening. But the primary difference is that all of it is happening at the same time. Tackling all of it at the same time is the unique thing now," he said.

NTPC in talks with Japan, South Korea, Germany for sale of green fuel India has outlined plans to become a major green hydrogen producer, even as developers worldwide have struggled to secure the long-term offtake agreements required to underpin large-scale investments

NTPC is in talks with prospective overseas customers as it develops a proposed green hydrogen hub in Andhra Pradesh | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters NEW DELHI 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 13 2026 | 12:39 PM IST

Listen to This Article

India's top power producer NTPC is in talks with potential buyers in Japan, South Korea and Germany for green ammonia and other low-carbon fuels, Chairman Gurdeep Singh said on Tuesday. India has outlined plans to become a major green hydrogen producer, even as developers worldwide have struggled to secure the long-term offtake agreements required to underpin large-scale investments. NTPC is in talks with prospective overseas customers as it develops a proposed green hydrogen hub in the southern state of Andhra Pradesh, Singh said at an event organised by the Indian Chamber of Commerce. The project is expected to produce green ammonia and green methanol, which are considered more practical than hydrogen for transportation and international trade.

"We have to make hydrogen a business," Singh said, adding that the focus was shifting from pilot projects to commercially viable ventures. Also Read

The comments underscore efforts by Indian companies to secure demand as they seek to turn government-backed hydrogen ambitions into commercially viable projects. Backed by subsidies of roughly $2.1 billion, New Delhi aims to produce 5 million metric tons of green hydrogen annually by 2030. Demand for green fuels is expected to rise as industries look for alternatives to fossil fuels to reduce missions and meet decarbonisation targets.

item.content:encoded:
Home / India News / India 'mother of democracy', does not grow at anyone's expense: PM Modi

India 'mother of democracy', does not grow at anyone's expense: PM Modi Citing India's linguistic diversity and digital reach, PM Modi said that technology, data and knowledge are redefining power, which should be used to empower people and create new opportunities

Prime Minister Narendra Modi addresses the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, in New Delhi | Image: PTI

Apexa Rai New Delhi 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 13 2026 | 11:30 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday said India does not believe in growing in isolation or withholding knowledge, but favours sharing its capabilities and working with other countries.   Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum , PM Modi said, “India does not grow at anyone's expense. We grow with the world and for the world."   Calling India the “mother of democracy”, PM Modi said the country’s linguistic diversity and wide-ranging media landscape reflected the many ways people access information and discuss issues.   He said India had more than 100 languages, around 80,000 registered newspapers and publications, and over 1,000 satellite television channels.   India's digital reach has further expanded the avenues for public discussion, he said, pointing to more than 500 million YouTube users and over 500 million Instagram users.

Also Read

“In our country, people openly debate different issues and discuss different perspectives,” PM Modi said, adding that digital power had played a significant role in enabling such exchanges.   He said power in the 21st century should be measured by how it is used and whether it benefits a wider section of society.   “The question is not who has power, but how that power is being used,” he said, highlighting the need to use knowledge to create opportunities rather than concentrate it in the hands of a few.   ALSO READ: PM Modi unveils ₹13K cr projects in TN, vows to work for state's growth

Affordable data has expanded access PM Modi also pointed to developments in India's digital ecosystem since 2014, saying affordable mobile data had helped extend access to digital services and learning opportunities.   He cited remote digital learning, online classes and the ability of shopkeepers in remote areas to use digital tools as examples of how connectivity could expand opportunities beyond major urban centres.
